def factor_boundary_settlement_premium_5d_20d_high(df):
    """Idea: Where closes settle relative to the broken 20-day high reveals whether the new level is being held; closes that finish well above the old boundary in the day's range indicate stronger acceptance.
    Logic: For each day with close above the prior 20-day high, express the close minus that resistance in units of the day's high-low range. Average this settlement premium over 5 days, and assign zero on days when price is not above the old boundary.
    Formula: mean_5( I(close > res20) * (close - res20) / (high - low) )
    Sub-mechanism tags: settlement premium, upper-bound hold, close-location relative to resistance.
    """
    df_copy = df.copy()
    prior_high = df_copy["high"].shift(1).rolling(20).max()
    day_range = (df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    settlement = (df_copy["close"] - prior_high) / day_range
    premium = np.where(df_copy["close"] > prior_high, settlement, 0.0)
    df_copy["factor_boundary_settlement_premium_5d_20d_high"] = pd.Series(premium, index=df_copy.index).rolling(5).mean()
    return df_copy["factor_boundary_settlement_premium_5d_20d_high"]
rationale: This factor focuses on where closes settle relative to the broken 20-day high rather than on the breakout move itself. A close far above the old boundary relative to that day's trading range signals strong acceptance of the new level, while a close hugging the boundary signals a weak hold. Averaging over five days makes the signal a durable settlement premium.
